chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from al-Nakha'i from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Jamil from some of our companions from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them): Regarding

a man who breaks his ritual purity (hadath) during the obligatory circumambulation (tawaf) and has already completed part of it, he said: 'He exits and performs ablution (wudu). If he has passed the halfway point, he builds upon his tawaf; and if he has less than half, he repeats the tawaf.' And whoever performs the voluntary tawaf and prays, then remembers that he was not in a state of purity, he should repeat the prayer, and there is no penalty upon him. This was narrated.

key_terms.رَجَعَ: Return/Repeat (implied in context of repeating prayer)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one breaks ritual purity during Hajj tawaf?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the 'halfway mark' (nisf) as the critical threshold for validity, reflecting the juristic principle that minor defects before completion can be remedied without restarting, while major defects require renewal. It distinguishes between the structural integrity of the tawaf itself and the validity of the accompanying prayer, highlighting the Shia emphasis on intention and awareness in ritual purity. This narration is foundational in the *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* for determining the precise moment a pilgrim must pause, purify, and resume or restart their circumambulation.
